judge_assessment.explanation: Every problem the judge names checks out. Problems 2 and 4 both end 'Write down the two points you read off the grid before you compute'; verify.json ids 2 and 4 are single slope entries (2 and -2) and the read-off points -- (0,3), (4,11) and (0,12), (5,2), which are the very coordinates the slope entries were built from -- appear in no check. Problem 3: 'Write an equation for the total cost, then use it to find the total cost after $8$ months' -- id 3 is one eval (15*m+20 at m=8 -> 140), so the equation is unrecorded. Problem 9: 'Write an equation for the seedling's height, then use it to predict the height after $9$ weeks' -- id 9 is one eval (3*w+12 -> 39 cm). Problem 12(b): 'Build the equation for the bill, then find how many gigabytes give a bill of $61$ dollars' -- id 12 carries a slope (5) and a solve ([8]) but no entry for the equation $b = 5g + 21$, and the intercept 21 appears only inside the solve expression. Second hard failure also confirmed: problem 7 ends 'name the graph the equation matches, and explain how the point you found proves it' and problem 11 ends 'state which of the two lines climbs faster and how you can see that on the grids without computing anything'; verify.json holds zero entries of type manual and machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags false. Note the naming half of problem 7 (the answer is Graph B) is a closed choice among three labelled graphs, so it is checkable rather than open -- it is unrecorded either way. All sixteen values recompute: 19, 5, 2, 140, -2, 7, 36, -12, 2, 5, 39, 19, 3, 4, 5, 8.

strengths_to_preserve: Four of the twelve ids already do per-slot verification correctly: ids 1, 6 and 10 each carry a read_data entry for the value the student reads and a separate slope entry for the rate, matching their two printed \ansline slots exactly, and id 12 carries a slope and a solve for its two parts. The pattern the sheet is missing elsewhere is one it demonstrates four times, which makes the fix a matter of consistency rather than new capability.

The three reference graphs are drawn once above problem 1 and called by letter, with an explicit note that the problems reference them -- so a value-bearing display is never sitting beside one problem where a student working the next one could apply it. The plotted functions and the verify points agree: Graph A is 2*x+3 and id 2's points (0,3) and (4,11) lie on it; Graph B is 12-2*x and id 4's (0,12) and (5,2) lie on it; Graph C is 4*x and id 11's (0,0) and (3,12) lie on it.

Problem 7 is the sheet's synthesis hinge and it is built well: substituting x = 5 into y = 12 - 2x gives the point (5, 2), and that point is visibly on Graph B and on neither of the others. The verification of the y-value is the evidence for the identification, so the two halves of the problem are genuinely one idea rather than two tasks stapled together.

Problem 12 is a real two-unknown extraction from two bills rather than a table with the intercept handed over: the rate comes from (2,31) and (5,46) and the fixed fee 21 must be recovered by back-substitution before the 61-dollar question can be answered. That is the one item on the sheet that cannot be done by pattern-matching a printed b.

root_causes.description: The coverage rule counts problem ids, not printed responses, so a two-instruction stem ('write an equation, then use it') is discharged by checking only the terminal number. The sheet proves the schema supports better -- ids 1, 6, 10 and 12 each hold several entries -- so the gap is that nothing FAILS when an id holds fewer entries than the item prints slots. SKILL.md line 189 and the coverage check in scripts/verify.py both stop at 'at least one check'.
evidence: worksheet.tex problems 3 and 9 both read 'Write an equation ... then use it to ...'; verify.json ids 3 and 9 hold one eval each
worksheet.tex problems 2 and 4 both read 'Write down the two points you read off the grid before you compute'; ids 2 and 4 hold one slope each
verify.json ids 1, 6, 10, 12 each hold two entries -- the same file therefore both demonstrates and violates the per-slot rule
SKILL.md line 189: 'verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check'

root_causes.description: Two interpretive responses (problem 7's 'explain how the point proves it', problem 11's 'how you can see that on the grids without computing anything') are the reasoning the interleaved-synthesis mode is meant to elicit, and neither is declared manual. SKILL.md line 257 prescribes manual for any explanation answer, but no gate checks for the imperative, so the sheet reports zero manual items and the pipeline treats the whole sheet as machine-verified.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7: '... and explain how the point you found proves it'
worksheet.tex problem 11: '... and how you can see that on the grids without computing anything'
verify.json: no entry has "type": "manual"; machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags is false

improvements.title: Equations and read-off points the sheet asks students to write are not verified
improvements.proposed_change: Add the missing entries following this file's own multi-entry convention: id 3 gains an equiv for the cost equation (15*m + 20); id 9 gains an equiv for 3*w + 12; id 12 gains an equiv for 5*g + 21; ids 2 and 4 gain read_data entries for the two grid points each ((0,3) and (4,11); (0,12) and (5,2)). Enforce it by extending tests/check_layout.py to count printed response slots -- \ansline, \answerline and \item subparts -- within each \problem segment and fail when the count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying that id.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 1 prints two \ansline slots with a verification JSON carrying a single entry for id 1; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming problem 1. It exits 0 today, which is the defect.
improvements.expected_impact: The equation-and-prediction facet is currently verified only at its output. A student who writes $y = 15m + 20$ correctly and then arithmetic-slips to 140 is indistinguishable from one who guessed, and the grader has nothing to bind against. Dominant systemic finding of the run (61 cases).
improvements.risk: Medium. The counter will misread graph-reading stems that mention points without printing a slot for them, and \ansline inside an enumerate needs to be attributed to the right problem. Land warn-only for one run and tune against this corpus.

improvements.title: Problems 7 and 11 ask for written graph interpretation and neither is declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual entry under id 7 (desc: 'the point (5, 2) lies on the drawn line of Graph B and on neither of the other two, so the substitution identifies the graph') and under id 11 (desc: 'Graph C is steeper -- for the same horizontal step it rises further -- so it climbs faster; accept any answer that compares steepness visually rather than by computing'). Split problem 7's graph identification out as its own checkable entry, since choosing among three labelled graphs is a closed answer. Enforce with the explanation-imperative lint in tests/check_layout.py.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem whose stem contains 'explain how' and whose id carries only an eval entry; assert the lint exits non-zero. No such lint exists today.
improvements.expected_impact: The sheet reports '12 verified, 2 manual' rather than a fully machine-verified claim it cannot support. Problem 11's comparison is the only item asking the student to reason from the picture instead of from arithmetic, which is what interleaved-synthesis is for.
improvements.risk: Medium; the imperative scan over-fires on directions prose. Warn-only first.

case_summary: A well-built representation-matching sheet: three shared reference graphs drawn once and called by letter, plotted functions that agree with the verify points, and a genuine two-unknown extraction at problem 12. Every one of the sixteen checked values recomputes. The rejection is right and the sheet is unusually instructive about the run's dominant defect, because it both demonstrates and violates the per-slot rule in the same file -- ids 1, 6, 10 and 12 each carry the right number of entries for the slots they print, while ids 2, 3, 4 and 9 each ask for two things and record one. Three equations the student is told to write ($15m + 20$, $3w + 12$, $5g + 21$) and four grid points they are told to read off appear in no check, and the two interpretive responses at problems 7 and 11 are inside a sheet reporting zero manual items. The fix here is consistency with a pattern the file already contains, not new machinery.
